sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax on a Victoria home?
sections.html:
Three separate offices touch a Victoria bill. The Victoria Central Appraisal District values the property, each taxing unit picks its own rate, and the Victoria County Tax Office mails the statement and takes the money.

Victoria had 66,500 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, up 1.5% from the 2020 base. The city covers about 37 square miles of land. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 put the owner-occupied housing rate at 57.9% and the median value of an owner-occupied home at $207,100. Those numbers explain why homestead rules matter here: most bills are on modest homes, so a fixed-dollar school exemption removes a large share of the school value.

The appraisal district's own page lists who does what. It determines values, mails notices of appraised value, handles protests and administers exemptions. The taxing entities set budgets and rates. The tax assessor-collector calculates and distributes bills and collects payment. A property inside city limits can owe tax to the county, the school district, the city and special units such as a junior college, hospital or road district.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address changes: Victoria Central Appraisal District, 2805 N. Navarro St., Suite 300, phone (361) 576-3621, open Monday to Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Bills, payments, penalty questions: the Victoria County Tax Office, 205 N. Bridge St., Suite 101, phone (361) 576-3671.
  • City rate and budget questions: the City of Victoria.

sections.h2: What is the Victoria city tax rate?
sections.html:
The city's 2025 rate was $0.4790 per $100 of taxable value, and the city's 2026 meeting notice proposed $0.4538. The City of Victoria posted a notice on September 9, 2026 saying it adopted a 2026 rate, so check the rate printed on your own bill for the final figure.

The city's meeting notice also sets out the voter-approval and no-new-revenue rates. It lists $0.4538 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.4652 as the voter-approval rate for 2026. The no-new-revenue rate is the rate that would raise the same tax from the same properties as the year before. The voter-approval rate is the highest the council can adopt without sending the rate to voters.

sections.h2: When is Victoria property tax due and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Victoria County tax statements go out in October, and the tax is due when you receive the statement. Payment is on time through January 31, and penalty and interest begin to accrue on February 1.

The county tax office explains the schedule this way: penalty starts at 6% on the first day of the delinquency month, rises 1% on the first day of each following month, and takes a final 2% step on July 1 for a total of 12%. Interest runs at 1% per month from the first day of delinquency. A payment mailed late in January counts only if the post office postmarks the envelope by January 31. The state Comptroller adds that a unit with an attorney contract can charge a further collection penalty of up to 20 percent on accounts that stay unpaid into July.

The state calendar matters for the year before the bill, too. Values are set as of January 1, notices of appraised value go out in spring, the appraisal district certifies its roll by July 25, and rates are adopted in late summer. The county tax office loads the certified roll and each unit's rate to produce the October statements.

  • If no statement arrives by November 1, ask the tax office to mail one. A missing bill does not change the due date or the lien.
  • If a mortgage company pays your tax, write your loan number on any statement you receive and send it to the lender.
  • Mortgage companies must request their clients' statements from the county by late August, or the owner may receive the bill directly.

sections.h2: How can a Victoria homeowner lower the property tax bill?
sections.html:
File a residence homestead exemption with the appraisal district, and protest the value if the notice looks too high. Both steps happen at the appraisal district, not at the tax office.

A home qualifies for the general exemption when it is the owner's main residence on January 1. Owners 65 or older get an additional exemption, and there are separate exemptions for disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. The state requires school districts to give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with an extra $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. A taxing unit may also adopt a percentage exemption of its own, so ask which local options apply to Victoria units.

Victoria CAD's exemption page lists what an applicant must supply under House Bill 585:

  • A copy of a Texas driver license or Texas ID card, with the property address matching the address on the license, vehicle registration or a utility bill.
  • A statement that no other homestead is claimed in or outside Texas.
  • Extra paperwork for a manufactured home, including a statement of ownership and location from the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs.

Active duty military members and their spouses can ask the chief appraiser to waive the address match. The exemption is not an annual application unless the chief appraiser asks you to reapply. Forms are on the district's Forms page, and the district takes completed exemption forms at exemptions@victoriacad.org. The general filing deadline is before May 1.

Homesteads also carry a state cap: the appraised value cannot rise more than 10% a year after the first qualifying year. Owners 65 or older or disabled can freeze the school tax amount on their home, and the freeze can move with them to a new Texas homestead.

sections.h2: How do I protest my Victoria appraisal?
sections.html:
File a notice of protest with the appraisal district by May 15, or within 30 days after the notice of appraised value is delivered if that is later. The district's taxpayer page links Form 50-132, a guide to filling it out, and the Comptroller's video on presenting a case.

The calendar on that page lists mid-April for the mailing of notices and May 15 for the protest deadline. The district accepts protests at protest@victoriacad.org. If the appraisal review board's order still looks wrong, the owner can go to district court, to regular binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value is over $1,000,000. Pay at least the undisputed tax before the delinquency date while any appeal is open.

sections.h2: How can I pay Victoria County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay in person at a county tax office, by mail, by phone or online. Partial payments are accepted, though any balance left after January 31 starts to collect penalty and interest.

  • In person: cash, check, money order, debit or credit card. A convenience fee applies to cards.
  • By phone at 877-253-4085, for Victoria County accounts only. The county lists a 2.30% card fee with a $1 minimum and a flat $0.50 fee for an electronic check.
  • By mail: write the account number and the words "partial payment" on a partial payment.
  • A returned check carries a $30 service charge.

Over-65 and disabled homeowners can ask about the state's four-installment plan, and a homeowner with delinquent taxes can ask the collector about a payment plan. Some collectors allow up to 36 months on a homestead, and a written request for waiver of penalty and interest must come within 181 days of the delinquency date under the state's rule.

sections.h2: What happens to Victoria property tax when I sell the house?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1 and follows the property, so the title company will settle the year's tax at closing. The county tax office tells new buyers to check their closing papers, because the title company may have collected from the seller and credited the buyer.

The owner on January 1 is the person the law holds liable for that year's tax, even after a sale. A buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid, so delinquent Victoria accounts are normally cleared from the proceeds. Ask the tax office for a statement of what is owed for each unit before you list. If a bill is behind, a buyer who pays cash can close with a title company that pays off the account, with the balance of the proceeds going to the seller.

New owners who buy after January 1 can claim the homestead exemption for the rest of that year if the prior owner did not receive it. Heirs who inherit a Victoria home without a recorded deed in their names need to give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to get the exemption.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Victoria city tax rate adopted?
faqs.a: The City of Victoria posted a notice on September 9, 2026 that it adopted a 2026 rate. The city's meeting notice proposed $0.4538 per $100, so confirm the final figure on your statement or with the tax office at (361) 576-3671.

faqs.q: When does Victoria property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1. Tax is due on receipt of the October statement, and a payment postmarked by January 31 is on time. After that, the county adds a 6% penalty plus 1% interest and keeps adding to the penalty monthly to a 12% ceiling on July 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Victoria property value?
faqs.a: Call the Victoria Central Appraisal District at (361) 576-3621. The county tax office sends bills but says the appraisal district makes every change to values, exemptions and account details.

faqs.q: Can I pay only part of my Victoria tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The county tax office accepts partial payments, but a balance still unpaid after January 31 accrues penalty and interest. Write the account number and the words partial payment on a check or money order.

faqs.q: Does a Victoria buyer owe the seller's unpaid tax?
faqs.a: The lien stays with the property, so unpaid tax has to be cleared before the buyer gets clear title. In practice the title company pays delinquent accounts from the seller's proceeds at closing, and the county tells new owners to check their closing papers.
